parsed.title: The Evidential THRESHOLD for Resurrection Belief - Gary Habermas
parsed.summary: This is an auto-captioned interview chapter in which Gary Habermas discusses historiographical method: he refuses to assign a numerical evidential threshold for historical facts, relies instead on categories of evidence (multiple attestation, eyewitness, early testimony), and treats strong evidence as far more important than scholarly consensus percentages. The material is almost entirely about historical apologetics methodology and does not engage the Theophysics axiom system; the only faint conceptual adjacency is to the requirement that claims be grounded in evidence and to the role of testimony/observation, but the source takes no stand on any canonical axiom node.

axiom_nodes.name: A5.1 — Observation Requirement
axiom_nodes.notes: Habermas appeals to eyewitness testimony and early accounts as strong historical evidence, which is conceptually adjacent to an observation requirement, but he is doing historiography, not asserting any axiom about observation grounding actuality.

axiom_nodes.name: BC1 — Terminal Observer Exists
axiom_nodes.notes: The discussion of eyewitnesses to the risen Jesus is thematically near the terminal-observer boundary condition, but the source makes no claim about a terminal observer in the axiom-system sense.
